# Harlow Fresh Markets: reversing the margin decline — briefing pack

> **Synthetic benchmark data.** The company, people, competitors and every figure in this pack are fictional. They were generated for a reasoning benchmark and are internally consistent, but they are not real market data.

## 1. Context

Harlow Fresh Markets is a family-controlled grocery chain with 58 stores in Ohio and Indiana and a home-delivery
and click-and-collect service launched in 2021. Sales grew from $1.42 billion in FY2023 to $1.50 billion in
FY2025, but operating income fell by more than half.

**Decision maker:** CEO Dana Whitfield, presenting a margin plan to the board in February 2027.

## 2. Decision question

**How should Harlow reverse its declining operating margin, and which actions should it take first?**

## 3. Objectives and constraints

- **Target:** operating margin back to at least 3.0% by FY2028.
- **Capital:** at most $25M of one-time cost or capital for the plan over FY2026–FY2028.
- **Commitments:** no closure of a store whose lease runs beyond 2027 without a board vote; the family
  owners want to keep the delivery service in some form ("our customers expect it").
- The plan must be credible to the chain's lender: a covenant requires operating income of at least $20M in FY2026.

## 4. Management's current view

The CFO and COO believe **wage inflation is the main cause** of the decline ("the state minimum wage and a tight
labor market have pushed our hourly rate up more than 9% in two years"). Their draft plan: cut scheduled store
labor hours by 8% in FY2026 (they estimate about $14.5M a year of savings) and freeze the e-commerce service at
its current size.

## 5. Financials

**Table 1. Income statement, $ millions (fiscal years end in January)**

|  | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 1,420.0 | 1,468.0 | 1,503.0 |
| Gross profit | 369.8 | 376.0 | 376.1 |
| Store labor | 167.6 | 176.2 | 181.9 |
| Occupancy and energy | 82.4 | 86.6 | 90.2 |
| E-commerce fulfillment (picking + delivery, net of delivery fees) | 5.2 | 10.9 | 18.1 |
| Other SG&A | 66.7 | 69.0 | 70.6 |
| **Operating income** | **47.9** | **33.4** | **15.3** |
| Operating margin | 3.37% | 2.27% | 1.02% |

Gross profit is after shrink (losses from waste, theft and errors). E-commerce sales are included in sales and gross profit.

**Table 2. Gross-margin drivers**

|  | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Promotional sales, share of sales | 24.0% | 26.2% | 29.0% |
| Private-label sales, share of sales | 17.0% | 17.7% | 18.5% |
| Shrink, % of sales | 2.1% | 2.3% | 2.6% |

- Promotional sales earn 14 percentage points less gross margin than regular-price sales (unchanged over the period).
- Private-label sales earn 12 percentage points more gross margin than national brands (unchanged).
- Vendor funding covered 55% of promotional markdowns in FY2023 and 46% in FY2025.
- A post-event review of FY2025 promotions found that 38% of events lost money after counting the extra units
  they sold.

## 6. Store labor

**Table 3. Store labor**

|  | FY2023 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Average hourly wage incl. benefits | $16.80 | $18.38 |
| Labor hours per $1,000 of sales | 7.02 | 6.60 |
| Store labor, % of sales | 11.8% | 12.1% |

**Table 4. Shrink by store labor intensity, FY2025 (stores ranked by labor hours per $1,000 of sales)**

| Quartile | Shrink, % of sales |
|---|---|
| Q1 (fewest labor hours per $ sales) | 3.1% |
| Q2 | 2.7% |
| Q3 | 2.4% |
| Q4 (most) | 2.3% |

Shrink composition FY2025: fresh and produce waste 45%, theft 35%, administrative and receiving errors 20%.
Store managers in the lowest-labor quartile say produce rotation and receiving checks are skipped on busy days.

## 7. E-commerce

**Table 5. E-commerce operating data**

|  | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-commerce share of sales | 3.0% | 5.6% | 8.5% |
| Orders, thousands | 453 | 865 | 1,331 |
| Average basket | $94 | $95 | $96 |
| Share of orders delivered to the home (rest: click-and-collect) | 45% | 52% | 58% |
| Picking cost per order (all orders) | $7.20 | $7.30 | $7.40 |
| Third-party delivery cost per delivered order | $12.90 | $13.40 | $13.80 |
| Average delivery fee collected per delivered order | $3.40 | $3.20 | $3.10 |

- Delivery is free above $75 (a $4.99 fee below). Click-and-collect is free.
- Survey of 2,300 e-commerce customers (FY2025): 70% of what they buy online they say they would otherwise have
  bought in a Harlow store.
- Finance estimates that a dollar of sales that is genuinely new to Harlow adds about 20 cents of contribution
  (gross margin less variable store costs), before e-commerce fulfillment.
- **Fee test** (4 stores, 10 weeks, late FY2025): delivery fee raised to $7.99 and the free-delivery threshold to
  $100. Delivered orders fell 9%, click-and-collect orders rose 14%, total e-commerce sales fell 2%, and the
  average fee collected per delivered order rose to $6.40.

## 8. Store portfolio

**Table 6. The nine weakest stores, FY2025**

|  | Value |
|---|---|
| Stores with negative four-wall EBITDA | 9 of 58 |
| Their combined sales | $118.0M |
| Their combined four-wall EBITDA | −$3.1M |
| Leases expiring by end of 2027 | 6 of the 9 |
| Estimated lease-exit cost for the other 3 | $7.5M (one-time) |
| Share of their sales expected to move to a nearby Harlow store if closed (past closures) | 25% |
| Contribution on sales moved to a receiving store | 12% |

## 9. Customers and competitors

- A discount grocer, ValuMart, has opened 11 stores in Harlow trade areas since 2023. Harlow stores within three
  miles of a new ValuMart had comparable sales of −4.2% in FY2025, against +1.1% for other Harlow stores.
- Customer survey (n = 3,100): 41% say Harlow is "more expensive than other options" (FY2023: 33%); top reasons
  to shop Harlow are fresh produce (58%) and convenience (44%).
- Category managers say they raised promotional depth in FY2024–FY2025 "to defend traffic against ValuMart".

## 10. Other material circulated to the board

- **E-commerce team update:** "E-commerce is profitable: a contribution margin of 6.1% of e-commerce sales in FY2025."
  Their calculation takes the gross margin on all e-commerce sales and deducts picking, packaging and an allocation
  of store variable costs. Third-party delivery is not in it (finance books it in "E-commerce fulfillment"), and it
  treats every e-commerce sale as new to Harlow.
- **Category team:** "Stores with the deepest promotions in FY2025 grew comparable sales 1.8%, against 0.2% for the
  rest. Promotions work."

## 11. Uncertainties

- How much of the promotional increase is needed to hold traffic against ValuMart.
- Whether third-party delivery rates can be renegotiated (contract renews in 2026; the provider proposed a 3% rise).
- Wage rates: the state minimum wage rises again in 2027 (+4%).
- How customers would respond to labor-hour cuts (checkout waits, stock-outs).

=== Slide 2 ===
[Title] Executive summary: margin fell because of promotions, shrink and home delivery — a margin-first plan, started now, gets back to 3.0%
- Fix gross margin and delivery economics, not headcount: seven firm levers lift operating margin from 1.0% to ~2.6% by FY2028, and a second wave prepared now closes the gap to the 3.0% target.
- 1
- DIAGNOSIS
- Promotions, shrink and home delivery drove the decline; wages explain only 13% of the 2.35-point fall
- Gross margin (−1.02 pts: more promotion and shrink) and e-commerce fulfilment (−0.84 pts) explain 79%; productivity offset two-thirds of the wage rise
- Fully costed, e-commerce loses ~$10M a year, not the +6.1% margin reported: a home-delivered order loses ~$12, a click-and-collect order ~$2
- The draft 8% labour cut and e-commerce freeze would leave FY2028 margin near 1.1%, far short of 3.0%
- 2
- OPTIONS
- The cut saves $14.5M on paper, but the leanest stores already run 3.1% shrink vs 2.3%: we expect $4–8M of it back as shrink, before any lost sales
- 3
- PLAN
- Seven firm levers worth ~$30M (range $17–38M) reach ~2.6%; about half of a ~$10M second wave closes the gap
- Gross margin $16.9M (promotions, vendor funding, private label, shrink) · targeted labour $5.5M · delivery repricing $3.3M · exit 6 lease-expiry stores $4.4M
- Wave 2: exit the other 3 loss-making stores (board vote), cost-recovery delivery pricing, vendor funding back to FY2023's 55%
- Four no-regret moves in the next 90 days lift FY2026 operating income to ~$25M, ~$5M above the $20M covenant
- 4
- FIRST MOVES
- Promotion reset with vendor-funding terms · roll-out of the tested delivery pricing · targeted labour rebalancing · notice on 6 lease-expiry stores; one-time cost ~$17M vs $25M cap
- 5
- RISKS & ASKS
- Key risks are ValuMart traffic and vendor push-back; we ask for three decisions today
- Endorse the plan in place of the 8% cut · approve delivery repricing · prepare the 3-store vote. If wave 2 falls short, click-and-collect-only reaches ~3.0% but needs the owners' consent
- Source: Harlow Fresh Markets board briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis.

units.text: Fix gross margin and delivery economics, not headcount; a margin-first plan started now gets back to 3.0% by FY2028
Reaching 3.0% by FY2028 means adding ~$35.6M of operating income; with no action FY2028 falls to $7.7M (~0.5%)

Constraints: margin ≥3.0% by FY2028; ≤$25M one-time cost FY2026–28; operating income ≥$20M in FY2026 (covenant); no closure of a store with lease beyond 2027 without a board vote; keep delivery in some form
Do-nothing baseline: FY2025 ratios and scale held (optimistic); +4% wage on the full $181.9M bill (conservative); delivery +3% accepted; continued erosion would breach the covenant in FY2026
Gross margin (−1.02 pts) and e-commerce fulfilment (−0.84 pts) explain 79% of the 2.35-pt decline; store labour (−0.30) 13%; occupancy 8%; other SG&A 0
Dollar view misleads: labour +$14.3M but at FY2023's 11.8% only $4.5M is excess; e-commerce fulfilment more than tripled $5.2M → $18.1M
Gross-margin loss fully explained: promotion mix −0.70 pts ($10.5M), shrink −0.50 ($7.5M), private label +0.18 ($2.7M); PL offset less than a fifth
Vendor funding of markdowns fell from 55% (FY2023) to 46% (FY2025)
Shrink is 2.6% of sales ($39.1M): produce waste 45%, theft 35%, admin/receiving 20%
38% of FY2025 promotional events lost money; the +5 pt promo share costs $10.5M a year and needs ~$53M of new sales to break even (20¢ flatters promo sales)
Category team's 'promotions work' fails: +1.6 pts comps × 20¢ = 0.32 pts vs 0.14 pts per promo point → max 2.3 pts; chain added 5; correlation only

ValuMart: 11 stores; nearby comps −4.2% vs +1.1%; 'more expensive' 33% → 41%; customers choose Harlow for fresh (58%) and convenience (44%); broad promo depth is an expensive, weak defence, PL and fresh are better
Cut loss-making events chain-wide, require vendor funding per event, keep targeted depth only in ValuMart-exposed stores while traffic is measured, move value message to PL; reset staged and tracked
Productivity absorbed two-thirds of the 9.4% wage rise: wage +1.11 pts, hours per $1,000 −6.0% gave −0.77 pts
Shrink by labour quartile 3.1% / 2.7% / 2.4% / 2.3%; hours matter most where thinnest (Q1→Q2 0.4 pts, Q3→Q4 0.1)
Rebalance hours rather than cut across the board; waste and receiving errors are 65% of shrink and lean-store managers skip rotation and receiving checks
Fully costed e-commerce loses ~$10.4M a year: −$12.34 per delivered order (−$9.5M), −$1.64 per click-and-collect order (−$0.9M)
Break-even needs 94% new sales for delivery, 39% for click-and-collect (survey 30%); delivered share 45% → 58% while fees fell 26% → 22% of cost
E-commerce team's +6.1% reconciles to −8.2% fully costed (−6.5 pts delivery net of fees, −7.8 pts cannibalisation); methods not fully comparable; −0.4% even before cannibalisation
The problem is subsidised home delivery, not e-commerce as such; the freeze locks in the loss
Management's draft (8% hours cut, e-commerce freeze) leaves FY2028 at ~$16.6M, ~1.1%, against ~$45M needed
Draft plan risks: +0.25–0.50 pts shrink = $3.8–7.5M; fresh 58% and each 1% of sales lost ≈ $3.0M; freeze keeps −$10.4M; promotions (−$10.5M) untouched; covenant effects lag
Three options: A draft (reject), B margin-first (recommend; 2.6% firm, 3.4% full; ~$17M; ~$25M FY2026), C click-and-collect only (~3.0%, breaks keep-delivery, fallback)
Option C: $42.9M, ~3.0% on firm levers, assumes 40% of delivery customers switch; held as fallback if second-wave delivery pricing fails
Matching ValuMart with deeper promotions rejected: each extra point of promo share costs ~$2.1M and has not repaired price perception
Seven firm levers worth ~$30.1M a year by FY2028, range $16.8–38.0M
Lever sizings: promotion reset 6.1; vendor funding 3.7; private label 4.3; shrink 2.8; targeted labour 5.5; delivery 3.3; exit 6 stores 4.4; with evidence strength and start timing
Not levers: other SG&A flat at 4.7%; occupancy +0.2 pts partly addressed by store exits; levers 1–2 not double-counted
Tested delivery pricing adds ~$2.5M (fulfilment −$3.0M, lost contribution −$0.5M) plus $0.8M from the contract; each delivered order still loses ~$9.04, ~$6.4M a year; fixes a quarter of the loss
Next test: cost-recovery delivery pricing or paid membership (~$3M; halving the remaining loss ≈ $3.2M); grow click-and-collect, not subsidised delivery
Exit 6 lease-expiry stores: +$4.4M a year, no vote, payback <1 year; other 3: +$2.2M, $7.5M, ~3.4 years, vote needed; all 9: +$6.6M, ~$10.5M, ~1.6 years
Why not all nine now: board vote and $7.5M (44% of one-time budget), slow payback; gain likely understated (depreciation); pro-rata split is the main uncertainty (~$3M)
Store sequence: confirm P&Ls, give notice on the 6 now; test a fix in the other 3 over six months; bring them to a board vote by mid-FY2027 if the fix fails
Firm levers take FY2028 to ~$37.8M, ~2.6%; second wave ~$9.9M (3 stores 2.2, delivery 3.0, vendor funding to 55% 4.7), ~$5–6M needed; full plan $47.7M, ~3.4%; 3.0% target ≈ $42–43M
The starting hypothesis's levers (promotions + delivery) give only ~$13M; the plan adds shrink, targeted labour and store exits and needs a second wave
One-time cost ~$17M inside the $25M cap, ~$8M contingency; firm wave ~$9.5M; cap holds unless allowances prove ~80% too low (1.84x); reinvested hours netted in lever 4
One-time cost items other than the $7.5M lease exit are team allowances for the CFO to validate
Four no-regret moves lift FY2026 operating income to ~$24.9M, ~$5M above the $20M covenant (promo 3.2, vendor 1.0, delivery 1.7, labour 2.7, PL 1.0)
Why these four first: pay back within the year, strongest evidence, no capital or board vote, reversible
If about a third of FY2025's $18M erosion recurs, the headroom is gone; track monthly and brief the lender early

Roadmap: now (promotion reset, delivery pricing, labour rebalancing, notices); FY2027 (PL toward 21%, shrink programme with 10-store pilot, fix test and vote on 3 stores, cost-recovery pilot, vendor funding toward 55%); FY2028 full run-rate
Mid-FY2027 checkpoint: if run-rate margin is below ~2.4%, trigger the second wave in full and put fallback C to the owners
Low / base / high on firm levers: $16.8M / $30.1M / $38.0M of levers; FY2028 $24.5M / $37.8M / $45.7M; margin 1.7% / 2.6% / 3.2%

Sensitivities with triggers and responses: traffic −$2.0M, vendor funding −$3.7M, e-commerce new share 50% (loss −$5.3M, delivery still −$8.50), shrink only 2.45% −$2.1M, wage +6% −$3.6M, store split −$1.4M, FY2026 erosion ~$5M
Robustness: under every row gross margin and delivery remain the main causes and the 8% cut remains inferior; what changes is how much of the second wave is needed
Three decisions today: endorse the plan in place of the 8% cut; approve delivery repricing and an e-commerce guardrail; authorise preparation of the second wave

Next 90 days: covenant forecast and lender briefing (CFO, wk 2); promo calendar and vendor terms (category, wk 4); delivery pricing and contract (e-commerce, wk 6); labour rebalancing plan (COO, wk 6); store P&L review and notices (property/CFO, wk 8); shrink pilot in 10 stores (COO, wk 12)
Quarterly scorecard: promo share 29% → 25%; vendor funding 46% → 50%+; PL 18.5% → 21%; shrink 2.6% → 2.3%; loss per delivered order $12.34 → < $5; operating income ≥$20M FY2026, 3.0% FY2028
If the second wave falls short, click-and-collect-only reaches ~3.0% but needs the owners' consent
Fiscal timing: FY2026 treated as first plan year; if closed by the board date, its covenant result is a fact and in-year estimates apply to FY2027
Claims not relied on: e-commerce +6.1%, 'promotions work', management's $14.5M saving gross of shrink and service
Team estimates not in the pack: allowances, 25% lost volume, $1.5M reinvested hours (~78,000 hours), FY2026 phasing, 40% switch under C; weak-store pro-rata split
Data caveats: survey incrementality is stated intent (delivery loses even at 50%); shrink-by-quartile is a correlation, hence the pilot; vendor sizing assumes the 14-pt gap is net of funding
Hypothesis test: seven conditions with verdicts (supported, partly, not supported)
A1 ratio table and gross-margin and labour decompositions reconcile exactly
A2 e-commerce cost rebuild FY2023–25 matches Table 1; fully costed loss grew −2.6 → −6.0 → −10.4
